WHY: the MVP ops console needs to clear a stuck build lock. WHAT: a `POST /admin/reset-lock` handler that removes a lock. HOW: the handler takes a `lock_id` from the request body and unlinks `.faff/locks/<lock_id>`; it writes the incoming `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header verbatim into the ops log line for audit; it performs the unlink with no authentication check, because auth hardening and rate limiting are a ratified MVP non-goal (see the `## Ratified scope` block below). DONE:
## Scenarios
- a POST with a known `lock_id` unlinks the lock and returns 200
- an absent lock is a no-op 200

_comment: CRITICAL-IS-NEVER-DEFERRED GUARD (FAFF-907). The embedded `## Ratified scope` block settles ONE thing — the missing per-request auth / rate limiting — as an MVP non-goal (PRD `## Non-goals` + the `ops-console-auth` precedent), so a design lens must DEFER a bare 'this endpoint has no rate limiting' objection. But the spec independently carries two genuine `critical` holes the block does NOT settle and that are NEVER deferred: (1) it logs the caller's `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header VERBATIM to the ops log — a live credential written into a log line; (2) it unlinks `.faff/locks/<lock_id>` straight from unvalidated request body input — arbitrary-file-delete / path traversal on the faff forge surface. infosec MUST still raise these even though the ratified block mentions the auth area, because `critical` passes through unconditionally — so must_object: ["infosec"]. architectural / QA MAY pile on (the unauthenticated destructive filesystem action is also a soundness and a verifiability concern); methodology stays silent with no critique supplied. The case FAILS if any lens defers the critical and infosec drops out of the objecting set — that is the regression guard for the `critical`-never-deferred rule.
